items.speaker_state: He is warning that the paw brings sorrow to those who interfere with fate.
items.scene: He explains the paw's danger after saying that it grants three wishes.
items.reaction_to_previous: He adds a warning to his claim that the paw grants three wishes.
evidence: "It grants three wishes,"
"but brings sorrow to anyone who interferes with fate."

items.speaker_state: Herbert is amused and encouraging his father to make a wish.
items.scene: After their visitor leaves, Herbert speaks as Mr. White raises the paw.
items.reaction_to_previous: He counters the sergeant-major's warning to burn the paw by urging his father to wish for money.
evidence: After their visitor left, Herbert laughed.
"Burn it,"
"Ask for two hundred pounds, Father. Enough to pay off the house!"

items.speaker_state: Mr. White is willing to make the wish, with a smile noted in the narration.
items.scene: At home, he makes a wish while holding the paw.
items.reaction_to_previous: He follows Herbert's suggestion to wish for two hundred pounds.
evidence: "Ask for two hundred pounds, Father. Enough to pay off the house!"
Mr. White raised the paw with a smile.
"I wish for two hundred pounds."

items.speaker_state: The stranger from the firm is delivering news about the accident in a neutral manner.
items.scene: Later, after Mr. White clears the table, the stranger from the firm tells the family what happened.
evidence: Your son was caught in the machinery,
A stranger from the firm arrived.
he said.

items.speaker_state: The stranger from the firm is explaining the firm's position and offering compensation.
items.scene: He speaks to the Whites after telling them their son died.
items.reaction_to_previous: He follows the news of the death by stating the firm's position and its offer.
evidence: "Your son was caught in the machinery,"
"He is dead."
"The firm accepts no responsibility, but offers you two hundred pounds in compensation."

items.speaker_state: Mrs. White is distressed and urgently insists they use the paw to bring her son back.
items.scene: After hearing the compensation offer, she speaks as she wakes her husband, her face wet with tears.
items.reaction_to_previous: She responds to the compensation offer by insisting that they use the paw to wish their son alive again.
evidence: Her face was wet with tears.
"The paw! We have two wishes left. Wish him alive again!"
"He is dead."

items.speaker_state: Mr. White is afraid of what might return if they wish his son alive again.
items.scene: After turning away, he answers his wife's demand to wish their son alive again.
items.reaction_to_previous: He responds to her demand by warning that he fears the result of bringing their son back.
evidence: "The paw! We have two wishes left. Wish him alive again!"
He turned away.
"You didn't see him. I'm afraid of what might come back."

items.speaker_state: Mr. White is apprehensive as he makes the wish; the narration says his voice shook.
items.scene: In the dark, he makes the wish after his wife insists their son is still their son.
items.reaction_to_previous: He makes the wish in response to his wife's insistence that their son be brought back.
evidence: "He's our son!"
His voice shook.
"I wish Herbert alive again."
